prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the continuous 3D geometry as the camera wearer turns right and approaches a raised wooden retaining wall topped with tall grass (moving from ~2–3 m on the right in frame 1 to within arm's reach at <1 m in frames 2–5), while a paved parking lot with cars (~8–30 m away) and apartment buildings (>30 m away) recedes to the left. In frame 1, a child stands directly in front of and below the camera wearer's eye level within arm's reach (~1–1.5 m away, lower body truncated by the bottom frame edge), and in frame 4 the top of a child's head reappears at the bottom edge (<0.8 m away, within arm's reach) just below the retaining wall corner while another small child stands ~2–3 m above and behind them in the tall grass on the upper slope. Across frames 3 to 5, the child standing in the grass on the upper slope (~2–4 m away and ~1–2 m above the parking lot level) is heavily occluded by surrounding grass blades and privacy blur in RGB. The depth map clearly reveals the continuous recession of the sloped embankment, the step-off of the retaining wall, and individual foreground grass blades in frame 5 (<0.5 m away) that blend together visually in RGB. However, the depth map is unreliable for the blurred child standing in the grass in frames 3–5, merging their silhouette almost completely into the surrounding vegetation depth plane rather than separating them as a distinct foreground surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete objects in the parking lot in frames 1 and 2, identifying a line of parked cars (~8–25 m ahead and to the left, spaced ~1–3 m apart, with the nearest red SUV at ~8–10 m partially leaving the left edge in frame 2) and the child in front of the camera wearer in frame 1 (~1–1.5 m away, facing right/three-quarters toward the wearer) and frame 4 (<0.8 m away at the bottom center edge, facing away/downward with only the top of the head visible). Both appearances of the nearby child are within arm's reach of the camera wearer and partially cut off by the bottom image boundary. In frame 1, the map helps separate overlapping distant vehicles in the lot and flags a small red object on the pavement (~6 m away on the left), though it mislabels that ground object as a 'person'. The map is highly unreliable in frames 3–5 as the camera turns toward the grassy embankment: it completely misses the retaining wall, trees, and buildings, fails to detect the blurred child standing ~3 m away in the grass in frame 3, and misclassifies that standing child in frames 4 and 5 (~2.5–3 m away, partly occluded by tall grass) as a 'bird'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D skeletal keypoints only in frame 1, detecting the head and shoulder alignment of the child standing ~1–1.5 m in front of and below the camera wearer (within arm's reach, lower torso and limbs out of view below the bottom edge). In frame 1, the facial and shoulder keypoints show the child's body angled slightly right while the head turns toward the right side of the frame rather than looking directly up at the camera wearer. A second cluster of yellow keypoints appears at the far right edge of frame 1 (which aligns with the boundary of frame 2), falsely hallucinating a compact body skeleton in the grass and retaining wall (~2 m to the right) or on a sliver of a person at the frame seam. The map makes the nearby child's shoulder axis and head orientation explicit despite the heavy privacy blur in the RGB image. However, the pose map is completely unreliable across frames 2–5, failing to detect both the close child's head at the bottom of frame 4 (<0.8 m away) and the second blurred child standing upright ~2.5–3.5 m away in the tall grass across frames 3–5.
